content: Sulfa allergies refer to adverse reactions caused by medications containing sulfa compounds. It is crucial to understand that the absence of the word sulfa in a medication's name, especially in generic names, does not guarantee that the medication is free of sulfa components. Antibiotics that contain sulfonamides include the following: Sulfamethoxazole Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (commonly known as Septra or Bactrim) Erythromycin-sulfisoxazole Two medications closely related to sulfonamides, which should be avoided by individuals with a sulfonamide allergy, are: Sulfasalazine (brand name: Azulfidine) Dapsone There are additional medications related to sulfonamides that should be used with caution. Although the risk of an allergic reaction is significantly lower with these drugs, it is essential to consult with a healthcare provider who can assess the risks and benefits. These medications include: Diuretics such as furosemide (Lasix) and hydrochlorothiazide (Microzide) Diabetes medications such as glyburide (Glynase, Diabeta, Micronase) and glimepiride (Amaryl) Certain nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as celecoxib (Celebrex) Migraine treatments like sumatriptan (Imitrex) Patients with HIV/AIDS may exhibit increased sensitivity to sulfonamides or medications similar to sulfonamides. It is important to note that sulfites and sulfates, which are commonly used as food preservatives, are unlikely to cause adverse effects in individuals with a sulfa allergy.
